title: Genesis ends (Genesis 49–50)
hook: Jacob's blessings, Joseph's forgiveness, and a coffin waiting to go home; finishing a book, the synagogue says "be strong"
tomorrow: a king who knew not Joseph

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ephraim: Jacob's crossed hands, and a blessing parents still say on Friday night. Your line was may you be like them. Today, the last page of the first book.

A synagogue on a Saturday morning in winter. The Torah scroll lies open on the table, and the reader is chanting the very last verse of Genesis. The whole book, from let there be light to here, is about to be finished. The moment the last word is sung, the whole room stands and calls out together, three words, loud: chazak, chazak, venitchazek. Be strong, be strong, and let us strengthen one another. It's a little like the cheer at the end of a long race.
screen: `THE LAST VERSE OF GENESIS.` → `THE WHOLE ROOM STANDS.` → `CHAZAK, CHAZAK, VENITCHAZEK.`

segments.voice: Jacob gathers his twelve sons and blesses them one by one. The blessings are honest: some praise, some hard words about old wrongs. He asks to be buried with his fathers in the cave of Machpelah, in Canaan, and he dies. Joseph and his brothers carry him home with a great Egyptian procession and bury him. Then, walking back to Egypt, the brothers get scared. Now that Father is gone, maybe Joseph will pay us back. They send him a message, and they fall down before him. Joseph weeps, and says: "Fear not; for am I in the place of God? And as for you, ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good." He'll take care of them, and their little ones. Years of peace after the reunion, and they still needed to hear it again. Sometimes forgiveness has to be said twice. Then Joseph grows old, and asks one thing: when God brings you out of here, carry my bones with you. And Genesis ends with this line: "and he was put in a coffin in Egypt." The book that began with a garden ends with a coffin in a foreign land, waiting to go home. That's where chazak comes in. It means be strong. The tradition says it at the end of every one of the five books of the Torah, and it fits here most of all. Something long is finished. The ending isn't tidy. And the next book begins in slavery. So before you turn the page: be strong, be strong, and strengthen each other.
screen: `JACOB BLESSES TWELVE SONS.` · `AM I IN THE PLACE OF GOD?` · `A COFFIN IN EGYPT.` · `CHAZAK: BE STRONG.` · then, large: `YE MEANT EVIL; GOD MEANT IT FOR GOOD.`

segments.voice: Look back at this part of the path: Rachel's grave, the coat, the pit, Tamar, the prison, the dreams, the cup, Judah, Ani Yosef, the grandsons. You finished it. Say the word, even quietly: chazak, be strong.
Chazak. Be strong. Called out in synagogue when a book of the Torah is finished: chazak, chazak, venitchazek.
Your line: be strong, be strong, and let us strengthen one another. One whole book of the Torah, done.

screen: `DAY 76 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A KING WHO KNEW NOT JOSEPH.`

howItsDone: When the reading of each of the five books of the Torah is completed in synagogue, the congregation stands and calls out chazak, chazak, venitchazek, and the reader repeats it.

notes: 'Seventeen years of peace': Jacob lived 17 years in Egypt (47:28). Confirm.
Chazak custom: congregation calls it out and the reader repeats it; Sephardi practice differs somewhat (e.g. chazak u-varuch at an aliyah). Confirm framing.
Link of chazak custom to Joshua 1 offered as an echo, not an origin. Confirm.
This day closes the Joseph part (days 64–76); the practice names the part's days.
